tools.name: read_workspace_document
tools.description:
Read content from a Google Docs document.

    Returns human-readable text by default. Use return_json: true for the raw Google Docs API response.

    Tabs: without tab_id or all_tabs this reads the first tab only. On a document with several
    tabs the result says how many there are and which one is shown. Pass tab_id to read one tab
    (sub-tabs are separate tabs), or all_tabs: true to read every tab in order under
    "## Tab: <path> [tabId: …]" headings; all tabs share one max_chars budget, and tabs past the
    budget are listed by id so you can read them with tab_id. On tab_id / all_tabs reads, smart
    chips, people and dates appear as their text, each list item (bulleted or numbered) starts
    with "• " (indented two spaces per nesting level, so an empty list item shows as a bare "•"),
    and headings start with [H1]…[H6], [Title] or [Subtitle]. These markers are not document
    text: leave them out of anchor_text and find_text. A Docs link containing ?tab=t.xxxx points at one tab; "t.xxxx" is its tab_id.

    Usage examples:
    
    1. Simple read:
       { "email": "user@example.com", "document_id": "1ABC123xyz" }
    
    2. With character limit:
       { "email": "user@example.com", "document_id": "1ABC123xyz", "max_chars": 10000 }
    
    3. Get raw JSON structure:
       { "email": "user@example.com", "document_id": "1ABC123xyz", "return_json": true }

    4. Read one tab:
       { "email": "user@example.com", "document_id": "1ABC123xyz", "tab_id": "t.abc123" }

    5. Read every tab:
       { "email": "user@example.com", "document_id": "1ABC123xyz", "all_tabs": true }
    
    Response includes:
    - Document title and URL
    - Text content (default: up to 50,000 characters)
    - Truncation indicator if content exceeds limit
    
    Note: For very large documents, consider using max_chars to limit response size.
    all_tabs cannot be combined with return_json; tab_id with return_json returns that one tab
    (up to 100,000 characters of JSON; sub-tabs listed by id; named ranges as a list, not keyed by name).

email.description: Email address of the Google account

document_id.description: Google Docs document ID (from URL or extract_workspace_document_id)

max_chars.description: Maximum characters to return (default: 50000). With all_tabs, one budget shared by all tabs.

return_json.description: Return raw Google Docs API JSON instead of formatted text (default: false)

tab_id.description: Tab id from list_workspace_document_tabs. "default" means the first tab.

all_tabs.description: Read every tab, in tree order (default: false). Not with tab_id or return_json.

tools.name: find_and_replace_workspace_document
tools.description:
Find and replace text throughout a Google Docs document.

    Without tab_id this replaces in every tab; pass tab_id to limit it to one tab (sub-tabs are
    separate tabs and are not included). A Docs link containing ?tab=t.xxxx points at one tab; "t.xxxx" is its tab_id.

    Usage examples:
    
    1. Simple replacement:
       { "email": "user@example.com", "document_id": "1ABC123xyz", "find_text": "old text", "replace_text": "new text" }
    
    2. Case-sensitive replacement:
       { "email": "user@example.com", "document_id": "1ABC123xyz", "find_text": "TODO", "replace_text": "DONE", "match_case": true }

    3. Replace a date placeholder in one tab only:
       { "email": "user@example.com", "document_id": "1ABC123xyz", "tab_id": "t.abc123", "find_text": "{{date}}", "replace_text": "2031-10-13" }
       Without tab_id a placeholder that also sits in a Template tab is replaced there too.
    
    Returns the number of occurrences replaced.
    Note: This replaces ALL occurrences of the text in every tab it covers.

email.description: Email address of the Google account

tab_id.description: Tab id from list_workspace_document_tabs. "default" means the first tab.

email.description: Email address of the Google account

include_word_count.description: Include word count for each tab (default: false)

return_json.description: Return the tab list as JSON instead of formatted text (default: false)

email.description: Email address of the Google account

document_id.description: Google Docs document ID or URL

tools.name: update_workspace_document_tab
tools.description:
Rename a tab and/or move it in a Google Docs document: reorder it among its siblings
    or nest it under another tab. A moved tab takes its sub-tabs with it. The API can't move a
    sub-tab back to the top level; re-create it there instead if needed.

    position is where the tab should end up (0 = first) among its siblings after the move; the
    numbers in list outputs start at 1. When nesting under another tab without position, the tab
    goes last. Titles must stay unique across the document. Needs a real tab id: "default" is
    refused. The result reports the tab's actual parent and position after the change.
    A Docs link containing ?tab=t.xxxx points at one tab; "t.xxxx" is its tab_id.

    Usage examples:

    1. Rename:
       { "email": "user@example.com", "document_id": "1ABC123xyz", "tab_id": "t.abc123", "title": "Archive 2031-10-06" }

    2. Reorder (make it the first of its siblings):
       { "email": "user@example.com", "document_id": "1ABC123xyz", "tab_id": "t.abc123", "position": 0 }

    3. Nest under another tab, as its first sub-tab:
       { "email": "user@example.com", "document_id": "1ABC123xyz", "tab_id": "t.abc123", "parent_tab_id": "t.def456", "position": 0 }

email.description: Email address of the Google account

tab_id.description: Tab id from list_workspace_document_tabs ("default" is not accepted)

title.description: New title (unique in the document, sub-tabs included)

parent_tab_id.description: Tab id to nest this tab under ("default" is not accepted)

position.description: Final position among the siblings after the move: 0 = first; the numbers in list outputs start at 1.

tools.name: list_drive_files
tools.description:
List files in a Google Drive account with optional filtering.
    
    Returns human-readable text by default. Use return_json: true for structured output.

    Usage examples:
    
    1. List recent files:
       { "email": "user@example.com" }
    
    2. List files in a folder:
       { "email": "user@example.com", "options": { "folderId": "1ABC123xyz", "pageSize": 50 } }
    
    3. Filter by query:
       { "email": "user@example.com", "options": { "query": "mimeType='application/pdf'", "pageSize": 20 } }
    
    4. List files in one shared drive (get the ID from list_shared_drives):
       { "email": "user@example.com", "options": { "driveId": "0ABCdef123" } }

    5. Get JSON output:
       { "email": "user@example.com", "return_json": true }

    6. Most recently modified first:
       { "email": "user@example.com", "options": { "orderBy": "modifiedTime desc", "pageSize": 10 } }

    Parameters (all inside "options"):
    - folderId: List contents of specific folder
    - query: Drive API query string
    - pageSize: Number of files to return
    - orderBy: Sort order, e.g. "modifiedTime desc" or ["folder", "name"] (Drive API orderBy keys)
    - driveId: Limit results to one shared drive (corpora is forced to 'drive')
    - corpora: 'user' (default), 'drive', or 'allDrives' (My Drive + every shared drive)

email.description: Email address of the Drive account

folderId.description: Optional folder ID to list contents of

pageSize.description: Maximum number of files to return

orderBy.description: Sort order, e.g. "modifiedTime desc" or ["folder", "name"] (Drive API orderBy keys)

driveId.description: Shared drive ID to list from (see list_shared_drives); corpora is forced to "drive"

corpora.description: Scope of the listing: "user" (default), "drive" (one shared drive), or "allDrives"

return_json.description: Return structured JSON instead of formatted text (default: false)

tools.name: move_drive_file
tools.description:
Move a file to a different folder in Google Drive.

Example: { "file_id": "abc123", "new_parent_id": "folder456" }

WORKFLOW: 
1. Use search_drive_files or list_drive_files to find the file_id
2. Use list_drive_files to find the target folder ID
3. Call this tool with file_id and new_parent_id

IMPORTANT: By default, this MOVES the file (removes from all current folders). 
To ADD to a folder without removing from existing folders, set remove_from_parents to an empty string.

email.description: Email address of the Drive account

remove_from_parents.description: Parent IDs to remove from, comma-separated. Default: fetches current parents (true move). Set to "" to add to folder without removing.
